pr_title: Fix lightmaps break when deferred rendering is enabled
pr_comments: Btw, maybe we should open another issue for the emissive issue?

The output of the deferred pass is already too large. We can't afford to include an additional attachment. I think the lightmap data should be stored in the emissive channel as it is essentially emissive.

> The output of the deferred pass is already too large. We can't afford to include an additional attachment. I think the lightmap data should be stored in the emissive channel as it is essentially emissive.

Good idea, the emissive object seems not need a lightmap, let me do some research and change the code.

Both the emissive and the light map need the extra precision and range from rgb9e5. My recommendation is actually to sum the emissive and light map into the emissive channel as light maps are essentially emissive.

You'd want to pre-multiply it by the diffuse color as seen here: https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/0c7df881e72c1167060c170b09e02586fc74d85f/crates/bevy_pbr/src/render/pbr_functions.wgsl#L551
Hi @DGriffin91 , I have used the emissive channel to transmit the lightmap data. Could you please review the code? Thank you.

Hi @JMS55 , I have synchronized my code with upstream and made necessary adaptations for the changes in the emissive's alpha channel. Now the lightmap works perfectly without the emissive issues we discussed earlier.
Hi @DGriffin91 , could you please help review these changes? Thank you.

issue_context.title: Lightmaps break when deferred rendering is enabled
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

Latest main

## Relevant system information

Windows 10

```
AdapterInfo { name: "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT", vendor: 4098, device: 29772, device_type: DiscreteGpu, driver: "AMD proprietary driver", driver_info: "24.5.1 (LLPC)", backend: Vulkan }
```

## What you did

- Go to the lightmaps example
- Add  `.insert_resource(Msaa::Off)` and `.insert_resource(DefaultOpaqueRendererMethod::deferred())` to the app.
- Add `.insert(DeferredPrepass)` or `.insert(ScreenSpaceReflectionsBundle::default())` to the camera.

## What went wrong

It looks like this:
![image](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/assets/23659539/573b706f-22d0-4f01-82d9-2156ef3a907d)

Other lights seem to work as normal.
comments:

Thanks for checking. Unfortunate bug, but not blocking for the release of 0.14 then.
